narrative:
The model determined that you have a 41% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability is high enough to cross the bank's threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this outcome were your credit history, the status of your checking account, and the level of savings you have. Your credit history of critical or other existing credits was the single most important reason for the denial. This history pushed the prediction strongly toward good credit risk; unfortunately the other two factors worked against you and outweighed that positive signal. 

Having a checking account balance between 0 and 200 DM was the second most influential piece of information. Only 18% of approved applicants fall into this bracket, while most approved borrowers have no checking account at all. This situation pulled the prediction noticeably toward bad credit. Your very low savings (under 100 DM) added further weight in the same negative direction. Nearly half of all applicants have similarly low savings, but the combination with your account status made the model view your overall financial buffer as too thin.

In short, although your credit history worked in your favor, the limited funds visible in your accounts created too much uncertainty for the bank.

What you should do next is focus on building a larger cash reserve and, if possible, clearing or consolidating any outstanding obligations so your credit picture looks cleaner. Once those areas improve, reapply and you are likely to receive a different decision. (218 words)
